questions.question: A solid cuboid is built from unit cubes. It is 4 cubes wide from left to right, 2 cubes deep from front to back, and 3 cubes tall. What does its front view look like?
options: A flat rectangle 4 squares wide, 3 squares tall
A flat rectangle 2 squares wide and 3 squares tall
A 3-D box sketch 4 wide, 3 tall and 2 cubes deep
A flat rectangle 4 squares wide and 2 squares tall
questions.explain: The front view uses the width and the height, so 4 wide by 3 tall. The common trap is grabbing the depth (2) instead of the width, which gives the side view.

questions.question: A solid cuboid is made of unit cubes. It is 5 cubes long from left to right, 3 cubes deep from front to back, and 2 cubes tall. What is its top view?
options: A 3-D drawing of the box seen from above at an angle
A flat rectangle 5 squares wide, 3 squares deep
A flat rectangle 5 squares wide and 2 squares tall
A flat rectangle 3 squares wide and 2 squares tall
questions.explain: Looking straight down you see length and depth, so the top view is 5 by 3. A top view is always flat, so any answer with slanted 3-D lines cannot be right.

questions.question: A solid cuboid built from unit cubes is 6 cubes long from left to right, 2 cubes deep from front to back, and 2 cubes tall. What is the view you get looking at it from the right-hand side?
options: A flat rectangle 6 squares wide and 2 squares tall
A 3-D sketch of the whole box, 6 long and 2 deep
A flat rectangle 2 squares wide, 2 squares tall
A flat rectangle 6 squares wide and 2 squares deep
questions.explain: From the side you see the depth and the height, so 2 by 2. The trap is using the 6-cube length, which belongs to the front view, not the side view.

questions.question: A solid cuboid is built from unit cubes. It is 3 cubes wide from left to right, 4 cubes deep from front to back, and 2 cubes tall. How many squares are in its top view?
options: 6 squares, because the top view is 3 by 2
24 squares, because 3 by 4 by 2 cubes are seen
8 squares, because the top view is 4 by 2
12 squares, because the top view is 3 by 4
questions.explain: The top view is width by depth, 3 by 4, which is 12 squares. Height never appears in a top view, and a flat view never counts all the cubes in the solid.

questions.question: On her desk Ava lines up 4 cubes in a single row from left to right, only 1 cube deep. She then stacks 2 more cubes on top of the cube at the far left. What is the front view of her model?
options: 4 squares in a row, with 2 extra squares above the left one
A 3-D sketch showing the 4 cubes and the 2 stacked cubes
A single row of 4 squares with no squares stacked above
1 square with 2 more stacked above it, 3 squares tall in all
questions.explain: From the front you see all 4 cubes across, and the left column is 3 high, so draw 4 squares with 2 more above the left one. The 1-wide, 3-tall shape is what you see from the side.

questions.question: For a class model Noah builds a bottom layer that is 3 cubes wide and 3 cubes deep, then puts a single row of 3 cubes on top along the back edge. What is the front view of his model?
options: 3 squares in a row with 1 more square above one end
A 3 by 2 rectangle of squares, 6 squares in all
A 3 by 3 square, because the base is 3 cubes by 3 cubes
A 3-D picture of both layers with the depth shown
questions.explain: From the front, every one of the 3 columns has a cube 2 high behind it, so the front view is a full 3 by 2 rectangle. The staircase shape with one raised end is the side view, and the 3 by 3 square is the top view.

questions.question: A display model at a science centre is a flat slab of cubes, 2 cubes wide from left to right, 4 cubes deep from front to back, and 1 cube tall. Ravi stands at the right-hand side and draws what he sees. What should his drawing be?
options: A row of just 2 squares side by side, 1 square tall
A rectangle 2 squares wide and 4 squares deep
A row of 4 squares side by side, 1 square tall
A 3-D sketch of the slab with its depth drawn in
questions.explain: From the side you see depth by height, so 4 squares across and 1 tall. Using the 2-cube width gives the front view instead, which is the most common mix-up.

questions.question: A solid is built from unit cubes. Its front view is a rectangle 3 squares wide and 2 squares tall, and its top view is a rectangle 3 squares wide and 1 square deep. What must its side view be?
options: A rectangle 3 squares wide and 2 squares tall
A 3-D box 3 long, 1 deep and 2 cubes tall
A rectangle 3 squares wide and 1 square deep
A rectangle 1 square wide and 2 squares tall
questions.explain: The top view gives a depth of 1 and the front view gives a height of 2, so the side view is 1 by 2. Copying the front view again is the trap, since the side view uses depth, not width.

questions.question: Sofia builds a tower model on her desk. The bottom layer is 4 cubes wide and 2 cubes deep. On top of that she covers only the 2 left-hand columns, full depth, and on top of that she covers only the far-left column, full depth. She now draws the view from the right-hand side. What should she draw?
options: A rectangle 2 squares wide and 3 squares tall
A staircase of squares 3, 2, 1 and 1 tall going right
A rectangle 4 squares wide and 2 squares deep
A 3-D sketch of the whole tower with its depth
questions.explain: From the right you see 2 columns of depth, and each one is hidden behind a stack 3 cubes high, so the side view is a full 2 by 3 rectangle. The 3, 2, 1, 1 staircase is the front view.

questions.question: In art class Emma builds a model from cubes and is asked for its top view. She draws a slanted box that shows the top face and two of the side faces. Her teacher says this is not a top view. Why not?
options: Because a top view must show the height of the model
Because a top view is flat, showing length and width
Because a top view is drawn from the right-hand side
Because a top view must be a net that folds into a box
questions.explain: A view is a flat drawing from one direction, so the top view shows only length and width, with no slanted depth lines. Sketching the solid in 3-D is the most common error here.

questions.question: Maya glues a cube model for a window display. The base is 4 cubes wide from left to right and 3 cubes deep from front to back, all 1 cube tall. She then stacks 2 extra cubes on the back-right corner cube. She draws the top view and the front view. How many squares does she draw altogether?
options: 17 squares, 12 on top plus 5 from the side view
16 squares, 12 on top and 4 in a single front row
18 squares, 12 in the top view and 6 in the front
30 squares, counting every cube face that shows
questions.explain: The top view is 4 by 3, which is 12 squares, and the front view is a row of 4 with 2 extra above the right column, which is 6, giving 18. Using 5 means the side view was drawn by mistake.

questions.question: Jayden's cube model is 2 cubes wide from left to right, 5 cubes deep from front to back, and 2 cubes tall. He says the front view is a rectangle 5 squares wide and 2 squares tall. What is his mistake?
options: He used the height, because he counted 2 cubes going up
He used a 3-D sketch, because he showed the depth lines
He used the top view, because he looked down at the model
He used the depth, so that is really the side view
questions.explain: The front view uses width and height, so it should be 2 by 2; the 5 comes from the depth, which belongs to the side view. Always check which measurement faces you before you draw.
